question: What happens if you place both page.tsx and route.ts inside the same app/dashboard/ directory?
options: Next.js merges them so GET returns HTML and POST returns JSON
Next.js throws a build/routing conflict because both files map to the exact same /dashboard URL segment
route.ts silently overrides page.tsx for all HTTP methods
page.tsx renders inside an iframe returned by route.ts
explanation: Both page.tsx and route.ts claim the same route segment URL, so Next.js forbids placing both in the same folder. Place API routes in app/api/... or separate folders.

question: Which HTTP status code should a POST Route Handler return when creating a new resource succeeds vs. when required JSON fields are missing?
options: 201 Created on success and 400 Bad Request when validation fails
200 OK on success and 404 Not Found when validation fails
204 No Content on success and 500 Internal Server Error when fields are missing
302 Found on success and 401 Unauthorized when fields are missing
explanation: 201 Created accurately signals that a new resource was persisted, while 400 Bad Request signals that the client submitted an invalid or incomplete payload.

question: When should you choose a Route Handler instead of a Server Action?
options: When submitting a standard HTML contact form inside your React UI
When triggering an optimistic like toggle inside a Client Component
When receiving a public webhook from a payment provider or serving a REST API for a mobile app
When reading initial data inside a Server Component page
explanation: Public webhooks, third-party integrations, and non-React clients require stable HTTP endpoints with explicit methods and status codes, which Route Handlers provide.

question: Why should a Server Component NOT call fetch('/api/notes') against its own app's GET Route Handler during server rendering?
options: fetch() is unavailable inside Server Components
Route Handlers cannot return JSON to Server Components
Server Components can only call POST endpoints, not GET endpoints
The Server Component already executes on the server and can call the shared data function directly without an extra HTTP round-trip
explanation: Calling your own Route Handler from a Server Component adds unnecessary HTTP serialization and network overhead when you can directly await the shared server data module.
